theory.overview: K-D Tree (k-dimensional tree) is a space-partitioning data structure for organizing points in k-dimensional space. Each node splits space along one dimension, alternating dimensions at each level. Enables efficient nearest neighbor search and range queries in O(log n) average time. Used in computer graphics, machine learning (k-NN), databases, and spatial indexing. This chapter covers K-D tree construction, search, and applications.

sections.title: K-D Tree Structure
sections.content: Binary tree where each node represents a k-dimensional point. At depth d, split along dimension d mod k. Left subtree has points with coordinate < split value, right subtree has ≥. Leaf nodes contain points or are empty. Height depends on insertion order. Balanced tree achieved by median split during construction.

sections.title: Construction
sections.content: Build tree by recursively splitting points. Choose median point along current dimension as root (ensures balance). Recursively build left and right subtrees on remaining points. Time: $O(n \log n)$ for balanced construction. Space: $O(n)$. Unbalanced construction: $O(n^2)$ worst case.
sections.algorithm: Choose median by current dimension. Recurse on left (points < median) and right (points ≥ median).

sections.title: Nearest Neighbor Search
sections.content: Find point closest to query. Recursively search down to leaf, track best distance. On backtrack, check if other branch could have closer point (if split plane is within best distance). Search other branch if needed. Time: $O(\log n)$ average, $O(n)$ worst.
sections.algorithm: Search down to leaf. On backtrack, check if other branch needs searching (split plane within best distance).

sections.title: Range Search
sections.content: Find all points in axis-aligned bounding box. Recursively check if node's region intersects query range. If intersects, recurse to children. If node's point is in range, add to result. Time: $O(n^{1-1/k} + m)$ where m is result size.
sections.algorithm: Check region intersection. If intersects, recurse. Add point if in range.

sections.title: K-D Tree vs Other Structures
sections.content: K-D Tree: efficient for low dimensions (k ≤ 10), dynamic updates possible. R-Tree: better for higher dimensions, disk-based. Quadtree/Octree: fixed 2D/3D, simpler but less efficient. Grid: simple but memory-intensive for sparse data. Choose K-D Tree for low-dimensional spatial queries.

keyConcepts.name: Alternating Dimensions
keyConcepts.description: Split dimension cycles through 0, 1, ..., k-1 as depth increases. Ensures balanced distribution across dimensions.

keyConcepts.name: Median Split
keyConcepts.description: Choosing median point at each level ensures balanced tree. Essential for efficient search.

keyConcepts.name: Bounding Box
keyConcepts.description: Each node represents a region (bounding box) in k-dimensional space. Used for pruning in range search.
keyConcepts.use: Prune branches that don't intersect query range

keyConcepts.name: Backtracking
keyConcepts.description: After reaching leaf, backtrack up tree checking if other branches could contain closer points (split plane within best distance).

steps.title: Choose Split Dimension
steps.description: Determine which dimension to split on (depth % k).

steps.title: Find Median
steps.description: Find median point by current dimension for balanced split.

steps.title: Create Node
steps.description: Create node with median point. Split points into left and right based on split dimension.

steps.title: Recurse
steps.description: Recursively build left and right subtrees with depth+1.
steps.code: node.left = build(left, depth+1); node.right = build(right, depth+1);

steps.title: Search
steps.description: For nearest neighbor: search down to leaf, backtrack checking other branches if needed.
steps.code: search(node, query, depth); if |query[split_dim] - node[split_dim]| < best: search(other_branch);

snippets.title: K-D Tree Node
K-D Tree Construction
snippets.code:
def build_kdtree(points, depth=0):
    if not points:
        return None
    
    k = len(points[0])
    axis = depth % k
    
    points.sort(key=lambda x: x[axis])
    median = len(points) // 2
    
    node = KDNode(points[median])
    node.left = build_kdtree(points[:median], depth + 1)
    node.right = build_kdtree(points[median+1:], depth + 1)
    
    return node  # O(n log n)
